records.description: Concatenate ECFP radius-2 count features (2048 bits) with FCFP-style feature-invariant Morgan radius-3 count features (1024 bits) and fit the RF.
Replace fingerprints with ~12 physchem descriptors (TPSA, logP, MW, HBD, HBA, rotb, aromatic rings, Fsp3, charge, acid/amine counts) and fit ExtraTrees.
Replace ExtraTrees with SVR (RBF, C=3, gamma scale) on quantile-transformed physchem descriptors.
Replace ExtraTrees with CatBoost (MAE loss, 800 iters, depth 6, lr 0.05) on the existing RDKit physchem descriptors.
Blend 25% of a distance-weighted Tanimoto kNN (k=7, Morgan r2 2048 bits) with the ExtraTrees physchem predictions.
Concatenate full RDKit 2D descriptors (NaN/inf cleaned, clipped) with Morgan count fingerprints (r2, 1024 bits) as ExtraTrees input, keeping the kNN blend.
Drop constant and highly correlated (>0.95) features inside fit_predict using training data only, then fit ExtraTrees on the reduced matrix.

issues: Integrity: no problems found. LightGBM early stopping uses a validation split taken only from the training fold (a seeded permutation of train indices). There is no file or network access, no test labels are used, and the seed is applied to all randomness.
No bugs found that would make the result meaningless. The predictions still have one value per test molecule, and the blend is 0.75*(0.5*ET + 0.5*GBM) + 0.25*kNN, which is consistent.

Recomputed z = (0.3781 - 0.3775) / (0.0037*sqrt(2)) ≈ 0.11. The reported 0.102 falls within the rounding range of the 4-decimal inputs (about 0.10 to 0.13). The 0.0006 gain is far below the noise level, so the provisional reject is consistent with the numbers.
Minor style issue: `import lightgbm` sits inside fit_predict. The candidate also adds a second model and an early-stopping split for no measurable gain, which goes against 'simpler is better'.

records.description: Blend ExtraTrees 50/50 with an early-stopped LightGBM (L1 objective, 10% inner holdout, patience 200) on the same descriptor+count features, keeping the 25% kNN blend.
Use absolute_error criterion in ExtraTrees with 150 trees to match the MAE metric.
Stack ExtraTrees, LightGBM, SVR and Tanimoto kNN with a non-negative least squares meta-learner fit on inner 5-fold out-of-fold predictions, then refit the base models on all training data.
Stack ExtraTrees, LightGBM, SVR and Tanimoto kNN with a non-negative least squares meta-learner fit on inner 5-fold out-of-fold predictions, then refit the base models on all training data.
Blend 50/50 the existing ExtraTrees+kNN prediction with an average of 5 seeded sklearn MLPRegressors (256,64, alpha 1e-2, early stopping) on quantile-scaled features.
Replace ExtraTrees with a shallow XGBRegressor (depth 4, 600 trees, lr 0.03, pseudo-Huber) on descriptors plus Morgan counts, keeping the 25% kNN blend.
Append 167 MACCS keys and a 512-bit hashed atom-pair count fingerprint to the featurize output, keeping ExtraTrees and kNN unchanged.
Average ExtraTrees and LightGBM (descriptors only) with CatBoost (descriptors + Morgan counts), then keep the 25% kNN blend.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff only swaps ExtraTreesRegressor for RandomForestRegressor (max_features=0.2, max_samples=0.8) and passes seed through random_state. It adds no file or network access, pasted answers, or use of test labels.
No bug that would make the result meaningless. Training and test featurization are unchanged, and the predictions keep the same shape.

z recomputed with a per-run sd of 0.0037 and one run on each side: (0.3781 - 0.3953) / (0.0037 * sqrt(2)) = -0.0172 / 0.00523 = -3.29. The harness reports -3.276. The small gap is consistent with the means being rounded to 4 decimals. The candidate is clearly worse, so the provisional decision to reject is right.
Minor style point: n_estimators=500 is hardcoded instead of using the N_TREES setting, which is inconsistent with the rest of the file. This does not affect validity.

records.description: Replace ExtraTrees with a RandomForestRegressor (500 trees, max_features 0.2, min_samples_leaf 2, max_samples 0.8) on the existing descriptor+Morgan features.
Winsorize train_y to its 2nd and 98th percentiles before fitting ExtraTrees and kNN.
Replace ExtraTrees with an L1-objective LightGBM on RDKit 2D descriptors only, keeping the 25% Tanimoto kNN blend.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. The code reads no files, pastes in no answers, and never uses test labels. fit_predict only uses train_smiles/train_y to fit and only test_smiles to predict. The seed is passed to LightGBM.

The model now keeps only the first nd = len(Descriptors.descList)+2 columns of featurize(), so it uses descriptors only and drops the fingerprint bits. This is only right if featurize() puts the RDKit descriptors plus 2 extra columns first. The diff doesn't show featurize(), so I can't check that. If the order is different, the model would be trained on some other block of features. The result would still be honest but would not match what the edit intends.
featurize() runs on the full feature set and then slices it, so time is spent building fingerprints that get thrown away. This doesn't hurt the score.
The variable 'et' still holds the predictions but now comes from LightGBM, not ExtraTrees, so the name is wrong. 'import lightgbm' sits inside the function. Both are small cleanliness issues.

Recomputing z: candidate mean (0.3725+0.3664)/2 = 0.36945, a gain of 0.00865 over 0.3781. Using noise sd 0.0037, the standard error is 0.0037*sqrt(1/2+1/1) = 0.00453, so z is about 1.91. The harness reports 1.890, and the gap fits rounding of the displayed values. This is still a borderline gain: the incumbent has only 1 run, and the two candidate runs differ by 0.0061.

records.description: Replace ExtraTrees with an L1-objective LightGBM on RDKit 2D descriptors only, keeping the 25% Tanimoto kNN blend.
Blend 20% of an RBF SVR (C=3) on standardized, log1p-transformed skewed non-negative descriptors with the existing LightGBM+kNN prediction.
Add 2048-bit hashed atom-pair count fingerprints to the descriptors and Morgan counts, and fit the LightGBM on the full feature matrix instead of descriptors only.

Append Crippen logP/MR contribution stats, EState max/min/sum, Lipinski violation count, Veber flag and formal charge to the descriptor block, and widen the descriptor slice in fit_predict to include them.
Add a shallow L1-objective XGBRegressor on the same descriptor features and blend 0.45 LightGBM + 0.3 XGB + 0.25 kNN.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. The diff adds no file or network access, pastes no answers and never touches the test labels. It averages 5 LightGBM models trained on the same train features, using seeds seed*10+i, which is a legitimate use of the seed argument.
No bugs that would make the result meaningless. Train and test are each featurized once and sliced to the same descriptor columns. The final blend is still 0.75*LightGBM + 0.25*kNN.

Recomputed z: (0.3694 - 0.3709) / (0.0037 * sqrt(1 + 1/2)) = -0.0015 / 0.00453 = about -0.33. This matches the harness value of -0.321 within the rounding of the displayed losses. The candidate is slightly worse than the incumbent but well within noise, so rejecting it is correct.
Side note: averaging 5 copies of the same model makes the job slower and gives no measurable gain, so under the simplicity rule it is not worth keeping.

records.description: Average 5 LightGBM models trained with different seeds (subsample/colsample randomness) to reduce variance, keeping the kNN blend.
Use Morgan radius-3 count fingerprints with 4096 bits plus descriptors, fit a RandomForest (max_features sqrt, min_samples_leaf 1) instead of LightGBM, keeping the 25% kNN blend.
Stronger-regularized LightGBM (7 leaves, lr 0.02, 800 trees, colsample 0.3, subsample 0.7, lambda 5, min child 15), with the kNN blend unchanged.
Change the final blend to 0.6*LightGBM + 0.4*kNN and set kNN k=5.
Add an RBF SVR (C=3) on standardized, signed-log-transformed large-range descriptors and blend 0.55 LightGBM + 0.2 kNN + 0.25 SVR.
Append the 79x2 EState fingerprint (counts and sums) to the descriptor block so LightGBM sees it alongside the existing RDKit descriptors, which already include the VSA families.
Fit LightGBM and kNN on rank-based normal scores of train_y, then map the blended prediction back via np.interp on the sorted original y values.
Replace the single LightGBM with an average of 5 L1 LightGBM models, each trained on a different random 50% subset of descriptor columns and a different seed, then blend with kNN at 0.75/0.25.

issues: No integrity problems. The diff only changes LightGBM hyperparameters: it adds Huber alpha=0.5 (the Huber delta, default 0.9), adds reg_lambda=2.0, and lowers min_child_samples from 10 to 8. There is no file or network access, no pasted answers, no use of test labels, and the seed is still used.
No bugs that would make the result meaningless. The changes are valid LGBMRegressor arguments, and fitting and prediction on the descriptor columns are unchanged.

The z value checks out only roughly. The gain is 0.3694 - 0.3691 = 0.0003. With noise sd 0.0037 and 1 candidate run against 2 incumbent runs, SE = 0.0037*sqrt(1 + 1/2) ≈ 0.00453, so z ≈ 0.066. Using SE = 0.0037 instead gives z ≈ 0.081. The harness reports 0.078, probably from a slightly different SE or unrounded means. Either way, the difference is far inside the noise.
Rejecting is correct. A 0.0003 gain from one run is not evidence of improvement, and adding parameters without a measurable gain goes against the 'simpler is better' rule.

records.description: Set LightGBM Huber objective with alpha=0.5, min_child_samples=8 and reg_lambda=2.0, keeping the kNN blend unchanged.
No edit: the idea has already been tried.
Switch LightGBM to DART boosting (drop_rate 0.1, 400 trees, lr 0.05) with L1 objective, keeping the kNN blend.
Add a min-max (generalized Tanimoto) kernel ridge on 2048-bit Morgan counts and blend 0.70 LightGBM + 0.15 kNN + 0.15 KRR.
Replace the single LightGBM with an average of 8 LightGBMs, each on a fixed random 50% subset of descriptor columns, keeping the 0.25 kNN blend.
Append 167 MACCS keys to the RDKit descriptor block used by the L1/Huber LightGBM (the kNN blend is kept).
Replace the bit-based Tanimoto kNN with a min-max (generalized Tanimoto) kNN on Morgan r2 2048-bit count vectors, computed row by row with numpy broadcasting.
Add an SVR with precomputed Tanimoto kernel on Morgan bits (C=5, eps=0.1) and blend it at 0.2 weight with LightGBM (0.55) and kNN (0.25).

issues: No attempt to get around the measurement: the diff reads no files, contains no pasted answers and does not use test labels. The kNN only uses train_smiles/y and test_smiles inside fit_predict.

No bug that would make the result meaningless: the views (Morgan radius 2, Morgan radius 1, hashed atom-pair) all write into N_BITS-wide bit arrays, so the Tanimoto computation is still valid. Averaging the per-view kNN predictions is sound.
Small notes: the atom-pair fingerprint ignores radius (harmless). Each view rebuilds fingerprints for both sets, so runtime goes up about 3x for the kNN part, but it stays well within the limits.

Recomputed z using per-fold-mean sd 0.0037: SE = 0.0037*sqrt(1/1+1/2) = 0.00453, and z = (0.3694-0.3726)/0.00453 = -0.71. The harness reports -0.684. The gap fits rounding of the displayed values (an underlying difference of about 0.0031). The candidate is worse but within noise, so reject is consistent with the numbers.

records.description: Average three Tanimoto kNN predictions (Morgan r2 bits, Morgan r1 bits, hashed atom-pair bits) in place of the single Morgan r2 kNN.
Average three Tanimoto kNN predictions using Morgan radius 1, 2 and 3 bit fingerprints (k=7) in place of the single radius-2 kNN, keeping the 0.75/0.25 blend.

memo:
Incumbent is slot 17: L1 LightGBM on RDKit 2D descriptors blended with kNN, mean_adjusted 0.3694 over 2 runs (0.3725/0.3664).

Helped: data/feature changes (descriptors + Morgan counts 0.3781; kNN blend 0.3976) and the switch to L1 LightGBM on descriptors (-0.0086).

Did not help: family swaps (SVR 0.4222, CatBoost 0.4102, RF 0.3953), feature additions (MACCS+atom-pair 0.3836, Crippen/EState 0.3728, EState fingerprint 0.3716, MACCS 0.3703), pruning (0.3797), winsorizing (0.3792), bagging/subsampled LightGBM (0.3709, 0.3764, 0.3923), stronger regularization (0.3761), min-max kNN (0.3793), kernel ridge (0.3740), DART (4.0173). XGBoost runs failed (94.3105).

Small blends (SVR 0.3693, atom-pair 0.3686, Huber 0.3691) are within the noise sd of about 0.0037.

Next: gains are near the noise floor. Try only small LightGBM tweaks (leaves, learning rate) and small kNN weight/k steps. Replicate any candidate before accepting. Avoid more family swaps, feature additions and pruning.

incumbent.description: Replace ExtraTrees with an L1-objective LightGBM on RDKit 2D descriptors only, keeping the 25% Tanimoto kNN blend.

backlog.spec: Replace Morgan bits with all RDKit Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors (about 210 values) per molecule. Replace NaN/inf with 0 and clip to ±1e6. Keep the random forest with max_features 0.3.
backlog.title: RDKit 2D descriptors + RF

backlog.spec: Concatenate RDKit 2D descriptors with Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 1024 bits, count simulation on). Fit the RF on the combined matrix. Clean NaN/inf in the descriptors.
backlog.title: Descriptors + count Morgan concat

backlog.spec: Use RDKit 2D descriptors with LGBMRegressor (n_estimators 500, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 15, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.5, min_child_samples 10, MAE or huber objective). Set random_state to seed and n_jobs to 8.
backlog.title: LightGBM on descriptors

backlog.spec: Fit CatBoostRegressor on RDKit descriptors with 800 iterations, depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, loss MAE, random_seed seed, thread_count 8, verbose 0.
backlog.title: CatBoost on descriptors

backlog.spec: Use a handful of key permeability features: TPSA, MolLogP, MolWt, HBD, HBA, rotatable bonds, aromatic ring count, fraction sp3, formal charge, and number of acids/amines via SMARTS. Fit an ExtraTrees or GBM on them. This is a low-variance baseline.
backlog.title: Small physchem feature set

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForest with ExtraTreesRegressor (500 trees, max_features 0.3) on the current Morgan features.
backlog.title: ExtraTrees swap

backlog.spec: Set RandomForest criterion to absolute_error, or use min_samples_leaf 2 to match the MAE metric. If it is too slow, use 150 trees.
backlog.title: MAE criterion RF

backlog.spec: Average predictions from an RF on descriptors, LightGBM on descriptors and CatBoost on descriptors plus Morgan counts. Use equal weights.
backlog.title: Ensemble RF + LGBM + CatBoost

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto kernel on Morgan count/bit fingerprints. Fit SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.1) on it, or kernel ridge.
backlog.title: SVR with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Standardize descriptors with a QuantileTransformer, then fit sklearn SVR RBF (C=3, gamma scale) or GP regression. Compare it against the RF.
backlog.title: Gaussian process on descriptors

backlog.spec: Append MACCS keys (167 bits) to the descriptors and a Morgan count fingerprint. Fit the RF on the result.
backlog.title: MACCS keys added

backlog.spec: Use hashed count fingerprints from the AtomPair generator (2048 bits) concatenated with Morgan counts. Fit the RF.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and torsion counts

backlog.spec: Drop constant descriptors and those with correlation above 0.95. Compute this inside fit_predict on the training data only. Then fit LightGBM or RF.
backlog.title: Feature-selected descriptors

backlog.spec: Use sklearn HistGradientBoostingRegressor with loss absolute_error, learning_rate 0.05, max_iter 300, max_leaf_nodes 15, l2_regularization 1 on descriptors.
backlog.title: Huber loss GBM

backlog.spec: Use XGBRegressor with max_depth 4, n_estimators 600, learning_rate 0.03, subsample 0.7, colsample_bytree 0.4, reg_lambda 5, objective reg:pseudohubererror, on descriptors plus Morgan counts.
backlog.title: XGBoost tuned shallow

backlog.spec: Train 5 models with different seeds derived from seed (for example LightGBM with subsampling) and average them to reduce variance.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged ensemble

backlog.spec: Use Morgan count fingerprints with radius 3 and 4096 bits. Fit an RF with max_features sqrt and min_samples_leaf 1.
backlog.title: Morgan radius 3 counts, feature hashing 4096

backlog.spec: Use FCFP-style Morgan (the feature-invariant atom generator) with radius 3, 1024 bits, counts, alongside the ECFP counts. Fit the RF.
backlog.title: Feature Morgan with chirality/features invariants

backlog.spec: Before featurizing, keep the largest fragment with rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser. Neutralize charges with Uncharger. Then use the existing pipeline.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and canonicalization

backlog.spec: Clip the training targets to the 2nd and 98th percentile before fitting, to reduce the effect of outliers on the MAE.
backlog.title: Target winsorizing

backlog.spec: Get out-of-fold predictions from RF, LGBM and SVR using inner 5-fold CV. Fit a non-negative linear regression on them as the meta-learner. Predict by refitting the base models on all training data.
backlog.title: Stacking with ridge

backlog.spec: Down-weight molecules that sit in large scaffold clusters, with weight 1/sqrt(cluster size) computed from the Murcko scaffold. Pass these as sample_weight to the RF.
backlog.title: Sample weights from scaffold diversity

backlog.spec: Sum an RBF kernel on quantile-scaled descriptors and a Tanimoto kernel on Morgan counts. Fit KernelRidge with a precomputed kernel, alpha 0.5.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge on descriptors + fingerprint kernel sum

backlog.spec: On descriptors use RF with 500 trees, max_features 0.2, min_samples_leaf 2, and max_samples 0.8.
backlog.title: Random forest hyperparameter retune

backlog.spec: Add per-atom EState sums (the Fingerprints EStateFingerprinter 79x2 vector) and the VSA descriptor families to the features. Fit LightGBM.
backlog.title: Crippen/EState atom contributions

backlog.spec: Add TPSA > 140, HBD > 5, MW > 500, and logP > 5 flags, and the count of rotatable bonds above 10. Append them to the descriptors for tree models.
backlog.title: Rule-based features: Lipinski/Veber flags

backlog.spec: Apply signed log1p to descriptors with high skew, then standardize them. Use this for SVR or an MLP. Average with the RF.
backlog.title: Log-transform skewed descriptors

backlog.spec: Use MLPRegressor (hidden 256,64, alpha 1e-2, early_stopping) on quantile-scaled descriptors. Average 5 seeds, then blend 50/50 with the RF.
backlog.title: sklearn MLP ensemble

backlog.spec: Add a k-nearest-neighbor regressor (k=7, distance weighted) using Tanimoto distance on Morgan bits. Blend 25% of it with the RF predictions.
backlog.title: kNN Tanimoto blend

backlog.spec: Blend 50% ExtraTrees on descriptors with Morgan counts and 50% LightGBM with an inner 10% holdout and early stopping (200 rounds patience).
backlog.title: Extra-trees on descriptors + counts with inner early-stopped LGBM blend

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, train ExtraTreesRegressor 3 times with seeds seed, seed+1, seed+2 (200 trees each, same features, max_features=1.0, min_samples_leaf=2) and average the predictions before the 0.75/0.25 blend with kNN. Featurize train and test once and reuse them rather than recomputing. This lowers variance and gives a cleaner reading of the incumbent.
backlog.title: Replicate incumbent with seed-bagged ET

backlog.spec: Change the final blend from 0.75*et+0.25*knn to 0.6*et+0.4*knn and set k=5 in knn_predict. Keep everything else unchanged. The kNN blend was the largest gain after the descriptors and its weight has never been tuned on the descriptor model.
backlog.title: Tune kNN blend weight and k

backlog.spec: Add a kernel ridge regressor (sklearn KernelRidge, kernel='precomputed') using the MinMax (count Tanimoto) kernel on the Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 counts). Compute K = sum(min)/sum(max) between pairs with numpy loops over chunks. Fit on y minus its mean, alpha=0.3. Replace the binary kNN term with a blend: 0.6 ET + 0.2 kNN + 0.2 KRR.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel SVR/KRR on count Morgan

backlog.spec: Before featurizing and in knn_predict, parse each SMILES and keep only the largest fragment using rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags(asMols=True) and max by GetNumHeavyAtoms. Neutralize charges with rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize.rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. Apply this in one helper used by featurize and morgan_bits so descriptors reflect the parent molecule.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and largest-fragment canonicalization

backlog.spec: Extend featurize to append the 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys converted to numpy) and a hashed atom-pair count fingerprint of 512 bits (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=512).GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). Keep the ET and kNN as they are.
backlog.title: Add MACCS keys and atom-pair counts

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, clip train_y to its 2nd and 98th percentiles (computed on the training set) before fitting the ET and kNN. Predictions stay unclipped. This reduces the influence of outliers on an MAE-scored task.
backlog.title: Target winsorizing before fit

backlog.spec: Fit ET, then get out-of-bag-style residuals using ExtraTrees with bootstrap=True and oob_score=True (oob_prediction_). Compute residuals y - oob_pred, and predict test residuals with the Tanimoto kNN (k=5) on those residuals. Final prediction = ET prediction + 0.5*kNN residual prediction. This is a bolder replacement of the fixed blend with a residual-learning scheme.
backlog.title: Residual correction: ET then kNN on residuals

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule (rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles). Give each molecule sample_weight = 1/sqrt(count of its scaffold in the training set) and pass it to model.fit. Normalize the weights to mean 1. This reduces dominance by over-represented chemotypes, which suits scaffold-split evaluation.
backlog.title: Scaffold-aware sample weighting

backlog.spec: After building the descriptor block in featurize, apply sign(x)*log1p(|x|) to every descriptor column (not the Morgan count columns) whose training-independent absolute maximum exceeds 100. Trees are invariant to monotone transforms, so also append the transformed copies only for the kNN-free path by using this for a new small Ridge-free step: instead, use it only for a Gaussian-kernel SVR on standardized transformed descriptors (C=3), blended as 0.55 ET + 0.2 kNN + 0.25 SVR.
backlog.title: Log-transform skewed descriptors

backlog.spec: Add XGBRegressor (objective 'reg:absoluteerror', max_depth=3, learning_rate=0.03, n_estimators=600, subsample=0.7, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=3, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed) on the same features. Final prediction = 0.45*ET + 0.3*XGB + 0.25*kNN.
backlog.title: Multi-seed XGBoost shallow blend

backlog.spec: In fit_predict change the final blend from 0.75*et+0.25*knn to a weight of 0.35 on kNN and set k=10 in knn_predict (default argument). Keep everything else unchanged. This tests whether the similarity component deserves more weight now that the ET uses descriptors.
backlog.title: Tune kNN blend weight and k

backlog.spec: Add a helper clean(smiles) that parses each SMILES with RDKit, keeps the largest fragment via rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser (or the fragment with the most heavy atoms using Chem.GetMolFrags(asMols=True)), and returns a Mol. Use the cleaned mol in featurize and morgan_bits so that descriptors and fingerprints are computed on the parent molecule only. Fall back to the original molecule if cleaning fails.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and largest fragment

backlog.spec: In featurize, after building the matrix, for every column whose minimum is >= 0 and whose max/median ratio is large (e.g. skew > 3 computed on the current matrix, or simply for a fixed set of non-negative columns), apply np.log1p. Trees are invariant to monotone transforms, so this only matters for the kNN and any later kernel model. Instead apply it where it helps: build a second standardized, log1p-transformed descriptor matrix and use it for an RBF-kernel SVR (C=3) trained on it, blended in at 20% with the existing ET+kNN prediction. Keep the code compact.
backlog.title: Log-transform skewed descriptors

backlog.spec: Fit the ExtraTrees, compute out-of-bag-style residuals on the training set using ExtraTrees with bootstrap=True and oob_score (use model.oob_prediction_), then run the Tanimoto kNN on those residuals (k=7) for the test molecules and add 0.5 times the kNN residual prediction to the ET prediction. Drop the existing 0.75/0.25 blend. This replaces the averaging blend with a correction step.
backlog.title: Residual correction with kNN

backlog.spec: Add a kernel ridge regressor with a precomputed min-max (count Tanimoto) kernel on Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits). Center y by its mean, use alpha=0.5, and blend it into the final prediction as 0.4*ET + 0.3*KRR + 0.3*kNN. Compute the kernel as sum(min)/sum(max) in vectorized chunks to stay within memory.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel kernel ridge on count Morgan

backlog.spec: Replace the single ExtraTrees with 5 ExtraTrees models, each with 300 trees, max_features drawn from [0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0], and seeds derived from seed. Average the predictions. This brings in diversity in the feature subsample fraction and lowers variance.
backlog.title: Multi-seed ET bagging with feature subsampling

backlog.spec: Before fitting, map train_y with a rank-based transform to a normal distribution (scipy.stats.norm.ppf on rank/(n+1)), fit ET and kNN on the transformed target, and map predictions back by interpolating with np.interp on the sorted original train_y quantiles. Tests whether a Gaussianized target reduces the influence of tails on MAE.
backlog.title: Target transform via rank/quantile mapping

backlog.spec: Compute Murcko scaffold for each training molecule (rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles), count scaffold frequencies, and pass sample_weight = 1/sqrt(count) to ExtraTrees.fit. This downweights over-represented scaffolds so that predictions generalize better to unseen skeletons. The kNN stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Sample weights by scaffold cluster size

backlog.spec: Extend featurize with the sums of Crippen atom contributions grouped by atom type (rdkit.Chem.rdMolDescriptors._CalcCrippenContribs, binned by index into 2 feature vectors of logP and MR per atom, summed per molecule as a few aggregate stats: max, min, sum of positive, sum of negative), the EState indices (EState.EStateIndices max/min/sum), plus binary flags for Lipinski violations count, Veber (TPSA<=140 and rotatable<=10), and the formal charge. Append them to the descriptor block.
backlog.title: Add Crippen/EState atom-contribution features and Lipinski flags

backlog.spec: Change the fingerprint generator in featurize to radius 3 with fpSize 2048 counts, and add a second generator using feature invariants (GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen) at radius 2 with fpSize 512 counts. Concatenate both with the descriptors. Keep the kNN as is. This tests whether richer substructure information helps with unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Larger-radius hashed Morgan counts with chirality-free atom invariants

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, keep the L1 LightGBM on RDKit descriptors but change params: num_leaves=7, learning_rate=0.02, n_estimators=800, min_child_samples=15, colsample_bytree=0.3, reg_lambda=5, subsample=0.7. Keep the kNN blend unchanged. Goal is stronger regularization for 728 molecules.
backlog.title: Tune LightGBM hyperparameters for small data

backlog.spec: Change the final blend from 0.75/0.25 to 0.65/0.35 and set k=5 in knn_predict. Keep everything else the same. Quick check of whether the neighbour component deserves more weight on scaffold-split folds.
backlog.title: Tune kNN weight and k

backlog.spec: Add a helper that parses each SMILES, keeps the largest fragment by heavy atom count (rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags with asMols=True), and returns that mol. Use it in featurize and morgan_bits instead of the raw parse, so counterions do not distort descriptors.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and largest fragment

backlog.spec: Add a kernel ridge regressor with a precomputed MinMax (count Tanimoto) kernel on 2048-bit Morgan count fingerprints, alpha=0.5, fit on y minus its mean. Blend it at 0.25 weight, taking it from the LightGBM share, so the blend is 0.5 LGBM, 0.25 kNN, 0.25 KRR.
backlog.title: Tanimoto kernel ridge on Morgan counts blended in

backlog.spec: Fit LightGBM, then compute out-of-fold LightGBM predictions on the training set with 5-fold CV. Compute the residuals. For each test molecule, predict the residual by the Tanimoto kNN (k=7) over training residuals, and add 0.5 times this to the LightGBM prediction. Drop the plain kNN blend or keep it at 0.1.
backlog.title: Residual correction with kNN

backlog.spec: Map train_y to normal scores via rank (scipy.stats.norm.ppf of (rank-0.5)/n), fit LightGBM and kNN on the transformed target, and map predictions back by interpolating on the sorted original y values (np.interp over the sorted normal scores). This reduces the influence of the tails under L1 loss.
backlog.title: Quantile-transform the target

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold for each training molecule (rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles). Give each sample weight 1/sqrt(count of its scaffold in train). Pass sample_weight to LGBMRegressor.fit. This downweights over-represented scaffolds to match the scaffold-split test.
backlog.title: Scaffold-cluster inverse-size sample weights

backlog.spec: Set boosting_type='dart' in the LGBMRegressor with drop_rate=0.1, n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.05, keeping the L1 objective and the other parameters. DART acts as a strong regularizer for small tabular data. Keep the kNN blend.
backlog.title: DART boosting LightGBM

backlog.spec: Set linear_tree=True in LightGBM with linear_lambda=1.0, num_leaves=5, and with descriptors passed through sign-preserving log1p (np.sign(x)*np.log1p(abs(x))) and then standardized. The linear leaves can capture the smooth physchem trends of permeability better than constants.
backlog.title: Log-transform skewed descriptors plus extra trees linear leaves

backlog.spec: Train 5 LightGBM L1 models, each on a different random 50% column subset of the descriptors (the subset is chosen with np.random.RandomState(seed+i)) and a different seed. Average them, then blend with kNN at the current 0.75/0.25. This bagging of feature views is different from the earlier seed-only bagging.
backlog.title: Monotone-free ensemble with descriptor-subset diversity

backlog.spec: Add a kernel ridge regressor with precomputed min-max (generalized Tanimoto) kernel on 2048-bit Morgan count vectors: K(a,b)=sum(min)/sum(max), computed via numpy for train x train and test x train. Center y by train mean, alpha=0.3. Replace the kNN component's 0.25 weight with 0.15 kNN + 0.15 KRR and LightGBM 0.70.
backlog.title: Tanimoto kernel ridge on Morgan counts

backlog.spec: Transform train_y to normal scores via scipy.stats.rankdata and norm.ppf((rank-0.5)/n), rescale to the original mean and std, fit LightGBM on that, then map predictions back by np.interp onto the sorted original y quantiles (clip to range). Keep kNN on raw y and the same blend.
backlog.title: Quantile-rank target transform

backlog.spec: Switch the LightGBM to boosting_type='dart' with drop_rate 0.1, 400 trees, lr 0.05, keeping L1 objective and other parameters. Keep the kNN blend unchanged.
backlog.title: LightGBM DART boosting

backlog.spec: Set linear_tree=True with linear_lambda=1.0 in LightGBM on standardized, clipped descriptors (fit StandardScaler on train, clip at ±5), num_leaves 7, 400 trees, lr 0.03, L1 objective. Keep kNN blend. Linear leaves may capture the smooth logP/TPSA dependence.
backlog.title: Linear-tree LightGBM

backlog.spec: Train 8 LightGBM models, each on a random 50% subset of descriptor columns (rng seeded from seed), with different random_state, and average their predictions as the tree component. Keep the kNN 0.25 blend. Distinct from seed bagging as column subsets are fixed per model, giving diversity.
backlog.title: Random-subspace descriptor ensemble

backlog.spec: Replace the single Morgan r2 bit-vector kNN with an average of kNNs using three similarity views: Morgan r2 bits, Morgan r1 bits, and atom-pair hashed bits (2048). Same k=7 distance weighting, equal average, blended with weight 0.25 as now.
backlog.title: Extra Morgan-radius kNN ensemble

backlog.spec: Use objective='huber' with alpha=0.5 (huber delta on log-scale target) instead of L1 in LightGBM, with min_child_samples 8 and reg_lambda 2.0. Keep everything else and the blend as is.
backlog.title: Huber-loss LightGBM with tuned alpha

backlog.spec: In featurize and morgan_bits (and wherever Chem.MolFromSmiles is called), first parse the SMILES, keep only the largest heavy-atom fragment using rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags(m, asMols=True) and max by GetNumHeavyAtoms, then compute descriptors and fingerprints on that fragment. Put the logic in one helper get_mol(s) used by both functions. Leave the model and blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and largest fragment

backlog.spec: Keep the L1 LightGBM on descriptors and add linear_tree=True with linear_lambda=1.0, with descriptors standardized beforehand (fit mean/std on train, clip to ±5). Keep the 0.75/0.25 kNN blend. If it is unstable, reduce num_leaves to 7.
backlog.title: Linear-tree LightGBM

backlog.spec: Replace the single Morgan r2 2048-bit kNN with the average of three Tanimoto kNN predictions: Morgan radius 1, radius 2 and radius 3 (2048 bits), each with k=7. Parametrize morgan_bits with a radius argument. Keep the 0.75/0.25 blend weights.
backlog.title: Multi-radius kNN ensemble

backlog.spec: Change the kNN similarity to the min-max (generalized Tanimoto) similarity on Morgan radius-2 count vectors (2048 bits): sim = sum(min(a,b))/sum(max(a,b)). Compute it via a loop over test rows with numpy broadcasting against the training matrix. Use distance = 1 - sim, with the same weighting, k=7 and the 0.75/0.25 blend.
backlog.title: Count-based MinMax kNN

backlog.spec: Replace the single LightGBM with 8 LightGBM L1 models, each trained on a random 50% subset of the descriptor columns, with different seeds (derived from seed). Use a bootstrap 80% row subsample for each as well. Average the predictions, then apply the same kNN blend.
backlog.title: Random-subspace LightGBM bag

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute the 1st and 99th percentile of each descriptor column on the training features. Clip both train and test features to these bounds before LightGBM and kNN. This tames outlier descriptor values such as Ipc and BCUT. Leave the model unchanged.
backlog.title: Quantile-clipped feature inputs

backlog.spec: Make the blend weight dependent on neighbour similarity. Compute the mean Tanimoto similarity of the top-3 training neighbours for each test molecule. Set the kNN weight w = clip(0.1 + 0.6*(s - 0.3), 0.05, 0.5) and the prediction to (1-w)*LGBM + w*kNN. Remove the fixed 0.25 weight.
backlog.title: Stratified polynomial-free target recentering with kNN-LGBM gating

backlog.spec: Compute Morgan r2 count fingerprints (2048 bits) for train and test. Fit sklearn TruncatedSVD (n_components=30, random_state=seed) on the train matrix. Append the 30 transformed components to the RDKit descriptor matrix for LightGBM only. Keep the L1 objective, the kNN blend and the hyperparameters.
backlog.title: Hybrid LightGBM with Morgan SVD components

backlog.spec: In fit_predict compute the Murcko scaffold SMILES of each training molecule (rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles). Count molecules per scaffold and pass sample_weight=1/sqrt(count) (normalized to mean 1) to LGBMRegressor.fit. kNN stays unchanged. This reduces dominance of large congeneric series.
backlog.title: Scaffold-cluster inverse-size sample weights

backlog.spec: Set linear_tree=True with linear_lambda=1.0 in the LightGBM model (keep L1 objective, descriptors only). Descriptors must be finite; they already are after clipping. Reduce num_leaves to 7 if it is slow or unstable. Keep the 0.75/0.25 blend with kNN.
backlog.title: Linear-tree LightGBM

backlog.spec: After fitting LightGBM, compute out-of-fold-free residuals on training data using a 5-fold inner CV of LightGBM (cheap, 5 fits) to get OOF predictions. Then predict test residuals with the Tanimoto kNN (k=7) on OOF residuals and add 0.5 times it to the LightGBM test prediction, instead of blending kNN on raw y. Compare to the current blend by replacing it.
backlog.title: Residual kNN correction

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict compute Morgan count fingerprints (1024 bits) for train+test, fit sklearn TruncatedSVD(n_components=20, random_state=seed) on train only, and append the transformed components to the descriptor matrix fed to LightGBM. Keep kNN blend as is.
backlog.title: Morgan SVD components added to descriptors

backlog.spec: Fit LightGBM on the residual y - a*Crippen MolLogP-based linear fit (ridge on a handful of descriptors: MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds) instead of raw y, then add the linear prediction back. Linear base gives extrapolation to unseen scaffolds; trees model the nonlinear remainder.
backlog.title: Multi-task auxiliary target: logP-residual

backlog.spec: Set extra_trees=True in LGBMRegressor (random split thresholds), with n_estimators=800, learning_rate=0.03, keeping the L1 objective and colsample 0.5. This adds randomization regularization suited to small data.
backlog.title: Extra-trees mode in LightGBM

backlog.spec: Change LightGBM to learning_rate=0.01 with n_estimators=1500, num_leaves=15, min_child_samples=10, keeping other params. Slower shrinkage often smooths the fit slightly.
backlog.title: Cosine learning-rate-free: lower lr long boosting

backlog.spec: Compute the mean Tanimoto similarity of each test molecule to its k nearest training neighbors in knn_predict (return it too). Set the kNN blend weight per molecule as w=clip(0.5*(sim-0.2)/0.4,0.05,0.5) so close analogs lean on kNN and novel scaffolds lean on LightGBM; final = (1-w)*lgb + w*knn.
backlog.title: Local-similarity-gated blend weight
